pages.title: Calendar
pages.text: The calendar records the current date, season, and month phase. Open the calendar tab in your inventory to see the current season.$(br2)A year has spring, summer, autumn, and winter, each divided into early, mid, and late months.

pages.title: Seasons
pages.text: Spring is March–May, summer June–August, autumn September–November, and winter December–February. Seasons are reversed between the northern and southern hemispheres.$(br2)The season changes temperature, rainfall, and snowfall.

pages.title: Climate Screen
pages.text: The Climate tab shows the local climate classification, geologic province, annual mean temperature, average rainfall, and current rainfall. Averages describe the long-term environment; current values describe the conditions around you now. See $(l:new_terra_earth/new_climate)New Climate$() for all 31 classifications and their distribution.

pages.title: How Temperature Is Calculated
pages.text: Local temperature combines the base climate, latitude and hemisphere, season, time of day, and elevation. Annual range describes seasonal change; daily range describes the difference between day and night. See $(l:new_terra_earth/annual_temperature)Annual Temperature Range$() and $(l:new_terra_earth/daily_temperature)Daily Temperature Range$() for detailed values.

pages.title: What Temperature Affects
pages.text: The final line of the Climate tab shows the combined current temperature. Temperature affects crops, fruit trees, bushes, and other plants, as well as snow and ice formation.

pages.title: Rainfall and Hydration
pages.text: Annual rainfall is measured in millimeters and ranges from 0~500 mm. Average rainfall affects flora, soil, and groundwater; current seasonal rainfall affects instant hydration. See $(l:new_terra_earth/rainfall_crops)Seasonal Rainfall and Crops$() for the conversion.

pages.title: Hemisphere and Elevation
pages.text: The default temperature scale is 20,000 blocks, and seasons are six months apart between hemispheres. Above Y=63, temperature cools with elevation, with the maximum reduction limited by the climate system. Leaf colors and seasonal models use the player's hemisphere.
